body:
So after some investigation and discussion with @stuartwdouglas the problem is identified - transformations are only supported in application archives, i.e. indexed artifacts.

You could see the following message when running the build with quarkus master:

> Cannot transform com.akamai.netstorage.NetStorage as it's containing application archive could not be found.

### Workaround - index third-party dependency

Just add the following two lines to the `application.properties` file:
```
quarkus.index-dependency.akamai.group-id=com.akamai
quarkus.index-dependency.akamai.artifact-id=NetStorageKit
```
As described here: https://stackoverflow.com/a/55513723/2654154

So first of all, thanks for your answer and the workaround! I still have some question, maybe you can shed some light on them.

Why is the indexing required for a bean which I produce in my artefact with a producer method? Quarkus should never ever need to call the init method in this case. I create the bean with another constructor. I'm now actually worried that Quarkus is creating the bean with the default constructor, which will definetively cause trouble. Shouldn't it be sufficient for Quarkus that the producer method is in my application?

> Why is the indexing required for a bean which I produce in my artefact with a producer method? 

So your producer is `@ApplicationScoped` which means that quarkus needs to create a _client proxy_ for the returned type (as defined by the CDI spec). Normally, a CDI container would fail with an error - because of the absence of a no-args constructor (which is a requirement for any normal scoped bean). In Quarkus, we do try to add a "synthetic" no-args constructor instead.

You could also annotate your producer with `@Singleton`. In this case, a client proxy is not required. But there are some drawbacks. For example you wouldn't be able to use the [new mocking functionality](https://quarkus.io/blog/mocking/).

OK, I see. Would it make sense/be possible for Quarkus to "auto-detect" the artefacts it needs to index in such a case? I mean during build time it should be possible to determine that this class is required for indexing and therefore this artifact needs to be indexed?
Stuart is already working on a fix - https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/pull/9105.

**Describe the bug**
I am working on the HiberanteRX extension for Quarkus, and as a part of that I have a bean that produces the type [`Mutiny.Session`](https://github.com/aguibert/hibernate-rx/blob/mutiny-publish-2/hibernate-rx-api/src/main/java/org/hibernate/rx/mutiny/Mutiny.java#L12) which is a concrete class with a 1-arg constructor:

```java
public class Mutiny {
	public static class Session {
		private RxSession session;
		public Session(RxSession session) {
			this.session = session;
		}
                // ...
        }
}
```

The producer bean can be seen here: https://github.com/aguibert/quarkus/blob/hibernate-rx-missing-ctor-issue/extensions/hibernate-rx/runtime/src/main/java/io/quarkus/hibernate/rx/runtime/RxSessionProducer.java#L30

The bean should produce objects like it does in JVM mode.
